summary: No missing positivity or distinct-degree assumption was found in the top-four envelope. Manuscript and canonical snapshot hashes match. The source distinguishes distinct points from possibly equal degree values.

checks.method: Inspected DegreeEnvelope's successive maximum-and-erase construction and integer envelope; exhaustively checked positive degree multisets of lengths four through seven with values one through five.
checks.observation: All 736 tested envelopes hold, including 710 cases with repeated top-four values. The source uses weak degree inequalities and erasure for point distinctness. Its explicit positive-degree premise guarantees nonnegative excess terms; all subtraction is integer subtraction. As a negative control, adding a zero-degree point to four degree-one points makes the proposed envelope read zero at most minus one. Actual support excludes precisely this failure, and support size at least 54 supplies four selectable points. The bounded enumeration corroborates, rather than proves, the universal lemma.
